structure_mechanism: compound-eye R1-R6 photoreceptors with refractory temporal sampling and rapid photomechanical rhabdomere contractions
claim: Drosophila can resolve moving spatial detail beyond the static sampling limit predicted from ommatidial spacing. Rapid photomechanical receptor movements narrow and shift receptive fields while saccadic image motion converts fine spatial structure into temporally separable signals.
biological_function: high-acuity tracking of moving image structure during natural saccadic viewing
limitations: Hyperacuity is motion- and state-dependent and does not mean that the static optical resolution of the compound eye has increased; transfer to other insect compound eyes requires direct testing.
popular_claim_correction: The result does not show that flies simply have more spatial pixels than ommatidia. Fine detail is recovered through active spatiotemporal sampling by moving/adapting photoreceptors.

sources.title: Microsaccadic sampling of moving image information provides Drosophila hyperacute vision
sources.authors: Mikko Juusola; An Dau; Zhuoyi Song; Narendra Solanki; Diana Rien; David Jaciuch; Sidhartha Anil Dongre; Florence Blanchard; Gonzalo G de Polavieja; Roger C Hardie; Jouni Takalo

structure_mechanism: pair of simple lateral camera-like eyes with under-focused optics and an unordered interdigitating rhabdomeric receptor layer
claim: A velvet worm demonstrates genuine but extremely coarse resolving vision despite an eye whose lens projects much of the image behind the retina. Behaviour, anatomy and optical modelling place spatial resolution at roughly 15-40 degrees, illustrating a visual system biased strongly toward sensitivity rather than acuity.
biological_function: orientation toward dark shelter and suitable microhabitat; fine prey or conspecific identification at distance is unlikely
limitations: The resolution estimate depends on assumed contrast sensitivity and experiments used ample photon availability; nocturnal performance and additional visual behaviours remain incompletely characterized.
popular_claim_correction: Similarity to ancestral panarthropod eyes does not make this a demonstrated living model of a Cambrian eye; evolutionary comparisons remain inferential.

sources.title: Low-resolution vision in a velvet worm (Onychophora)
sources.authors: John D Kirwan; Josefine Graf; Jochen Smolka; Georg Mayer; Miriam J Henze; Dan-Eric Nilsson

structure_mechanism: grouped retina with photonic-crystal-lined reflecting cups containing cone bundles and rods positioned behind the cups
claim: The elephantnose fish retina deliberately pools photoreceptors into reflecting macroreceptor units: photonic-crystal cups boost and spectrally redistribute light so rods and cones operate together over dim conditions, while spatial pooling suppresses fine spatial noise. The system therefore favors reliable detection of large moving signals in turbid water over conventional acuity.
biological_function: rapid detection of large biologically relevant moving objects, including predator-like stimuli, in dim turbid freshwater
limitations: The specialization reduces spatial detail and should not be described as generally superior vision; Gnathonemus also relies heavily on active electrolocation, and performance depends on its particular turbid habitat.
popular_claim_correction: The fish is not simply 'almost blind' nor do its photonic crystals create high-resolution night vision. The retinal architecture intentionally sacrifices spatial clarity to improve robust low-contrast object detection.

sources.title: Photonic Crystal Light Collectors in Fish Retina Improve Vision in Turbid Water
